sub.hardware: Hardware read from Windows interfaces. Choose your gaming GPU and display here.
sub.memory: Installed modules, effective data rate and memory use. XMP/EXPO state cannot be verified through Windows.
sub.cpu: Processor topology, power policy and a measured idle load.
sub.gpu: GPU, driver and graphics settings. Driver panel settings need manual verification.
sub.display: Every connected monitor, the active refresh rate and supported modes.
sub.windows: Windows gaming settings, power state and informational security state.
sub.storage: Drives, free space and the health Windows reports.
sub.network: Adapter details and a latency test that runs only when you start it.
sub.bios: Read only. This app never writes to BIOS/UEFI. Settings it cannot verify are shown as such.
sub.monitor: Real measurements only. Monitoring stops when you leave this page.
sub.sessions: Idle load is measured first, then you start your game. FPS is not measured.
sub.safe: Nothing changes by default. The changes below are backed up and undone with one click.
sub.advanced: Only verified settings can be edited. Others are shown as unavailable.
sub.profiles: Profiles hold hardware-independent preferences. Exported files contain nothing machine-specific.
sub.backup: A snapshot is taken before every Apply. The original baseline is created once and never changed.
sub.reports: Operation reports, the application log and exports with a privacy review.
welcome.title: Welcome to BF6 Universal Optimizer
welcome.body: This app identifies your hardware, audits your Windows gaming configuration and offers previewed recommendations for Battlefield 6 settings.
welcome.safety: Nothing changes without your approval. A backup is taken before every change. No administrator rights, drivers or background services are needed.

sub.servers: Regional latency, live monitoring, route analysis and server IP management. Region tests measure AWS network probes, not Battlefield game servers.
net.fallback_note: ICMP got no reply; measured over TCP and excluded from ranking.
net.no_reply_note: {0} of {1} attempts got no reply. This is not game packet loss.
net.refreshed: {0} targets stored, {1} invalid entries rejected. ip-ranges check: {2}.
net.refresh_failed: The target list could not be fetched or its format changed. Last valid targets are kept.
net.probe_warning: These addresses are AWS region probes, not verified Battlefield servers. The list is not an official EA server inventory. A missing reply does not mean in-game packet loss.
net.best_disclaimer: This is the lowest-latency tested regional endpoint, not necessarily the Battlefield 6 matchmaking server or the region with the lowest in-game ping. The app cannot steer matchmaking.
net.jitter_formula: Jitter: the mean absolute difference between consecutive valid RTTs. Missing replies are not counted.
net.thresholds: Upper limits for Excellent / Good / Fair (ms). App-defined, not an EA standard.
net.thresholds_invalid: Thresholds must be positive and ascending.
net.live_note: Measures once per second and stops when you leave the page. Red lines are samples with no reply.
net.live_summary: Average {0} ms · Peak {1} ms · Jitter {2} ms · Timeouts {3} · Interruptions {4} · Duration {5}
net.route_note: A silent router is not proof of packet loss. Intermediate routers do not show the physical location of a Battlefield server.
net.route.no_data: No hop replied, so no conclusion is possible.
net.route.not_reached: The target did not reply to ICMP. This does not mean it is down.
net.route.jump: Lasting delay increase at hop {0}: about {1} ms. This may be long distance or a carrier change.
net.route.high: Last hop latency is high: {0} ms.
net.route.silent: Some hops did not reply; this is normal and is not loss.
net.route.ok: No clear problem on this route.

If you know the server IP, add it in IP Manager.

term.xmp.name: XMP
term.xmp.text: Intel's memory profile standard. It lets the module's rated speed be selected in BIOS. Windows cannot read its state reliably.
term.expo.name: EXPO
term.expo.text: AMD's DDR5 memory profile standard, enabled in BIOS like XMP.
term.mts.name: MT/s
term.mts.text: Million transfers per second. DDR5-6000 means a 6000 MT/s data rate on a 3000 MHz clock.
term.vrr.name: VRR
term.vrr.text: Variable refresh rate: the display follows the frame rate (G-SYNC, FreeSync).
term.hags.name: HAGS
term.hags.text: Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling. Its effect varies by system; it is not universally good or bad.
term.vbs.name: VBS
term.vbs.text: Virtualization-based security, a Windows protection. Being enabled is not a fault.
term.commit.name: Memory commit
term.commit.text: The total memory Windows has promised to programs. The limit is RAM plus pagefile.

check.ram_pressure.title: Memory pressure

check.ram_commit.title: Memory commit
check.ram_commit.advice: Nearing the limit can cause application errors. Do not disable the pagefile.
check.ram_pagefile.title: Pagefile
